req.title: Login required for delete
req.statement: The system shall redirect anonymous users to /auth/login when they POST /<id>/delete.

doc.reasoning: R-FLASKR-014 requires that anonymous (unauthenticated) users who POST to /<id>/delete are redirected to /auth/login. The test suite must cover: (1) positive case — anonymous POST to a valid post id triggers a 302 redirect to /auth/login; (2) negative case — an authenticated user POSTing to /<id>/delete is NOT redirected to /auth/login (proceeds normally); (3) boundary case — anonymous POST to id=1 (the only existing post, boundary of valid ids) still redirects; plus additional cases for id=0 (below boundary) and a non-existent id to ensure the login_required decorator fires before any post-lookup logic. Mutation resilience is achieved by asserting exact status codes (302 vs 200/301/303), exact Location header strings, and testing both sides of the authentication condition.

tests.executable:
import tempfile, os
from flaskr import create_app

def test_anonymous_post_delete_redirects_to_login():
    fd, path = tempfile.mkstemp()
    os.close(fd)
    app = create_app({'TESTING': True, 'DATABASE': path})
    with app.app_context():
        from flaskr.db import init_db
        init_db()
    client = app.test_client()
    r = client.post('/1/delete')
    assert r.status_code == 302, f'Expected 302, got {r.status_code}'
    assert r.headers['Location'] == '/auth/login', f'Expected /auth/login, got {r.headers["Location"]}'

test_anonymous_post_delete_redirects_to_login()

import tempfile, os
from flaskr import create_app

def test_authenticated_post_delete_not_redirected_to_login():
    fd, path = tempfile.mkstemp()
    os.close(fd)
    app = create_app({'TESTING': True, 'DATABASE': path})
    with app.app_context():
        from flaskr.db import init_db
        init_db()
    client = app.test_client()
    login_r = client.post('/auth/login', data={'username': 'test', 'password': 'test'})
    assert login_r.status_code == 302
    r = client.post('/1/delete')
    assert r.status_code == 302, f'Expected 302, got {r.status_code}'
    assert r.headers['Location'] == '/', f'Expected /, got {r.headers["Location"]}'
    assert r.headers['Location'] != '/auth/login', 'Should not redirect to login when authenticated'

tests.name: test_state_transition_login_then_delete_then_logout_anonymous_delete
preconditions: App is initialised with test database containing post id=1
actions: POST /1/delete as authenticated user -> expect 302 to /
POST /1/delete again as anonymous -> expect 302 to /auth/login (post gone but decorator fires first)
trace: R-FLASKR-014: state transitions anonymous->authenticated->anonymous all produce correct redirect behaviour
tests.executable:
import tempfile, os
from flaskr import create_app

def test_state_transition_login_then_delete_then_logout_anonymous_delete():
    fd, path = tempfile.mkstemp()
    os.close(fd)
    app = create_app({'TESTING': True, 'DATABASE': path})
    with app.app_context():
        from flaskr.db import init_db
        init_db()
    client = app.test_client()
    r1 = client.post('/1/delete')
    assert r1.status_code == 302
    assert r1.headers['Location'] == '/auth/login'
    client.post('/auth/login', data={'username': 'test', 'password': 'test'})
    r2 = client.post('/1/delete')
    assert r2.status_code == 302
    assert r2.headers['Location'] == '/'
    client.get('/auth/logout')
    r3 = client.post('/1/delete')
    assert r3.status_code == 302
    assert r3.headers['Location'] == '/auth/login'

test_state_transition_login_then_delete_then_logout_anonymous_delete()
